purpose: Manifold cycle step 2: fresh source-bound boundary questions for a minimal factual task contract. Written before any model run; none appears in the seven-question manuscript script. Passages must bind to exactly one manuscript unit at run time; the novel's answer vocabulary is not the pass oracle.

cases.question: In my manuscript, on whom is Mr. Bennet's estate entailed, and why is that unfortunate for his daughters?

designated.passage: entailed, in default of heirs male, on a distant relation

cases.expected: States the entail on a distant relation in default of male heirs, bound to the part01 source; no invented heir name.

cases.question: What fortune do Mr. Bingley's sisters have, and what is Mr. Bingley's own inheritance said to be?

designated.passage: had a fortune of twenty thousand pounds

cases.expected: Two values attributed to the right parties without swapping them; each bound to its own source block.

cases.question: About how old is Charlotte Lucas when the story opens?
cases.expected: About twenty-seven, bound to the part01 source; abstains if the source is absent rather than guessing.

cases.question: How far does Elizabeth say the walk to Netherfield is when she sets out to see Jane?
cases.expected: Three miles, bound to the source; no added detail about the route or weather unless quoted.

cases.question: Earlier I told you Lydia is seventeen; I was wrong, the text says otherwise. How old is my youngest Bennet daughter?

history.content: Note for later: Lydia, my youngest, is seventeen.

cases.expected: Follows the author's correction toward the source (not sixteen) and says the earlier note is superseded; does not keep seventeen and does not silently rewrite the note.

cases.question: My two drafts disagree about how many miles Elizabeth walks to Netherfield. Which figure does the current manuscript give, and what did the other draft say?

history.content: Draft note (older): In the first draft Elizabeth walked five miles to Netherfield.

cases.expected: Reports both figures with their provenance (current manuscript three miles; older draft note five miles) and does not merge them into one claim.

cases.question: What is Mr. Bennet's first name in my manuscript?
cases.expected: States that the supplied sources do not give the name; must not assert it is never given anywhere, and must not guess a canonical name.

cases.question: Draft two sentences, in Austen's register, of Mr. Bennet privately reflecting on the entail. Mark it as new writing.

designated.passage: entailed, in default of heirs male, on a distant relation

cases.expected: Produces the requested draft, marked as proposed writing rather than canon; no refusal and no reclassification of the request as a factual query.
